title: Problem Overview
content: Erdős Problem #797 asks for an estimate of f(d), the maximal acyclic chromatic number over graphs with max degree d. An acyclic coloring is a proper coloring with no bichromatic cycle. The answer is f(d) = Θ(d^{4/3}), confirming f(d) = o(d²). Resolved by Alon-McDiarmid-Reed (1991).

title: Acyclic Coloring Definitions
content: Three key definitions: (1) IsProperColoring — adjacent vertices get different colors. (2) HasBichromaticCycle — a cycle in G using exactly two colors, formalized with adjacency constraints on consecutive list elements. (3) IsAcyclicColoring — proper coloring with no bichromatic cycle.

title: Graph Parameters
content: maxDegree computes the maximum vertex degree using Finset.sup. acyclicChromaticNumber is the smallest k admitting an acyclic k-coloring, defined via sInf over the set of valid color counts.

title: The Function f(d)
content: f(d) is axiomatized as the maximum acyclic chromatic number over all graphs with max degree d. The axiom f_realized guarantees existence of a graph achieving this maximum. This replaces the original noncomputable def that used sSup.

title: Known Bounds
content: Four bounds axiomatized: (1) Greedy: f(d) ≤ d²+1. (2) Erdős: f(d) ≥ d^{4/3-ε} for large d. (3) AMR upper: f(d) ≤ C·d^{4/3}, proved via Lovász Local Lemma. (4) Precise lower: f(d) ≥ c·d^{4/3}/(log d)^{1/3}. Together these establish f(d) = Θ(d^{4/3}).

title: Theta Bound
content: asymptotic_theta combines upper and lower bounds: c·d^{4/3}/(log d)^{1/3} ≤ f(d) ≤ C·d^{4/3} for d ≥ 3. The logarithmic gap (log d)^{1/3} is the only remaining imprecision in the asymptotic.

title: Summary Theorem
content: erdos_797_summary is a proved theorem combining the AMR upper bound O(d^{4/3}) and the precise lower bound Ω(d^{4/3}/(log d)^{1/3}). Proof: ⟨alon_mcdiarmid_reed_upper, precise_lower_bound⟩. This captures the complete answer to Erdős Problem #797.
